notes: PHASE-000 foundation is complete and PHASE-001 development is active. WU-002 remains in progress because its acceptance criterion is not yet satisfied: approved desktop calling applications have not consumed processed/bypass audio through an installed OS-visible VSN virtual microphone. The verified Windows foundation includes Rust audio contracts and bounded queues, deterministic device selection/reselection, bounded stream recovery, IAudioClient3 planning, event-driven WASAPI capture, sample decode/reframing, CaptureRuntime reopen recovery, IMMNotificationClient delivery, bounded virtual-mic staging/output, Rust/C++ transport ABI, aligned Interlocked cursor publication, deterministic shared-region geometry, real user-mode section mapping and a WDK-buildable KMDF control driver with a secure driver-owned section lifecycle. The caller-supplied-section CONNECT assumption was replaced by driver-owned CONNECT v2 in merge 3953069f468c46d744f30625b3696e5b12f03a77. The KMDF control-driver slice merged as b2761ad400d92c1d810751fabcf4b071a40dfb9c. Protocol v2 then added an aligned per-slot seqlock stamp and the guarded ConsumeOneRingFrame contract; AI Native run 34541120876 and Windows run 34541120903 passed before merge 9c57207482bdc20ca5dc70a06cbb43c0cfa86741. The PortCls/WaveRT descriptor slice established a build-valid 48 kHz mono 32-bit IEEE-float single-capture-stream descriptor set with wave bridge, host capture pin, ADC node and minimal microphone topology; AI Native run 34542011551 and Windows run 34542011553 passed before merge da1b0543bcbfe63ff6a342690cab3b250057bbe2. The subsequent PortCls lifecycle/WaveRT stream-contract slice adds real compile/link references to PcInitializeAdapterDriver and PcAddAdapterDevice while keeping StartDevice fail-closed with STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED until real miniport registration exists. It also adds a bounded WaveRT runtime contract whose STOP/ACQUIRE/PAUSE/RUN values are compile-time matched to KSSTATE, validates buffer/block/notification geometry, tracks cyclic and monotonic linear byte positions, accumulates notification cadence, resets state on STOP, rejects advancement outside RUN and keeps overflow failures transactional. The same state mapping and probe compile in the real WDK .sys target; the user-mode regression executable verifies transition ordering, wraparound, notification cadence, invalid geometry/advances, paused behavior and both linear/notification overflow paths. AI Native Quality Gates run 34543128712 and Windows Audio Validation run 34543128651 both passed on implementation head 54da66c1aa78f913d98ac98faaa9a8d56e4dcdf7; Windows passed Rust compile/Clippy/tests, pinned WDK restore, .sys build/WDK validation and the expanded C++ suite. This slice merged as 78ef04bf86bf02b25b9da25ef401dc84f73f0f2b. The live DriverEntry still uses the previously verified normal-KMDF PnP control-device path and intentionally does not call PcInitializeAdapterDriver yet. PortCls must own the audio PnP dispatch path, so the next valid WU-002 action is to refactor the secure IOCTL surface into a WDF control device compatible with WdfDriverInitNoDispatchOverride/PortCls ownership, retaining the driver-owned section, requestor ownership and cleanup semantics. After that refactor is build-verified, switch DriverEntry to PortCls-primary initialization while StartDevice remains fail-closed; then implement/register the actual wave/topology miniports and WaveRT stream bound to ConsumeOneRingFrame. No OS-visible endpoint claim is valid until INF/install/enumeration/runtime evidence exists. Still pending are live PortCls DriverEntry, real miniport/stream registration, guarded-ring scheduling integration, INF/package installation/test signing, endpoint enumeration/runtime DeviceIoControl evidence, least-privilege non-admin runtime policy, approved calling-app routing, physical-device recovery evidence, hardware CPU/latency/jitter/deadline measurements, and production signing/update/uninstall/rollback verification. Paid provider usage, proprietary model training, production credentials/cloud spend and production deployment remain subject to applicable provider/data/compute/release gates.
